extracted.intended_audience: Attorneys and practitioners who appear before the USPTO (particularly trademark practitioners), respondents in OED disciplinary proceedings, and USPTO enforcement staff.
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing acceptance of an Affidavit of Resignation and exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, including related obligations (notice to clients, limited recognition, account suspensions) and the professional-conduct rules alleged to have been violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit of resignation and exclusion on consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, the USPTO Director has the authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the legal basis for approving the respondent's Affidavit of Resignation and for issuing the Final Order excluding the respondent from practice in all matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director approved the Affidavit because it 'complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a).' Compliance is a prerequisite to approving exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent must be freely and voluntarily rendered
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent must acknowledge that her consent is freely and voluntarily rendered in making the Affidavit, and that she is not being subjected to coercion or duress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit must include an express statement that consent is voluntary; absence of voluntariness may affect the approval of exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of pending investigation (37 C.F.R. § 11.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must acknowledge awareness that the OED Director opened an investigation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.22 concerning alleged violations of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit should show the respondent knows an investigation is pending and the nature of the allegations being investigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of factual allegations/summary of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit should acknowledge (and the Final Order summarizes) the underlying factual allegations (e.g., respondent's relationship with Logicize, processing of raw files, hiring a non-practitioner assistant, creation and submission of OBJ files, impermissible signing and submission of applications—530 applications/filings impermissibly signed and submitted, failure to inform clients and the Office).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit need not admit guilt but must acknowledge the allegations and the factual circumstances that led to the disciplinary matter; the Final Order documents those facts for the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent representation — 37 C.F.R. § 11.101
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must provide competent representation; OED alleges violations by 'not applying the USPTO trademark signature rules,' 'not using other signature methods,' and 'not informing her trademark applicant clients of the actual or potential adverse consequences' of impermissible signing, in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence includes knowing and applying USPTO signature rules and advising clients of adverse consequences; failure may support disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable diligence and promptness — 37 C.F.R. § 11.103
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness; OED alleges failure by 'failing to take reasonable steps to ensure that her clients' trademark filings were reviewed, signed and filed in accordance with the U.S. Counsel Rule and the trademark signature rules' and by not informing clients of adverse consequences, in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligence includes implementing processes to ensure filings comply with rules and promptly notifying clients of problems; systemic failures (e.g., hundreds of improperly signed filings) are cited as violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision of non-practitioner assistants — 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.503(a) and (b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must adequately supervise non-practitioner assistants; OED alleges violations by not adequately supervising her non-practitioner assistant and/or Logicize, allowing impermissible entry of applicants' signatures and filing of improperly signed documents, in violation of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.503(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervision obligations include ensuring assistants do not perform unauthorized practice or improperly execute signature/filing steps; failure to supervise can be a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misrepresentation — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving misrepresentation; OED alleges impermissibly entering the direct signature of applicants (or allowing others to do so) on applications and declarations and filing them, in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly entering a client's signature or allowing others to do so without authorization is treated as misrepresentation and triggers disciplinary concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not engage in conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice; OED alleges that entering direct signatures and filing improperly signed documents (and failing to inform the Deputy Commissioner) adversely affected the integrity of the federal trademark examination and registration process, in violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions that undermine the trademark examination/registration process or harm its integrity can constitute conduct prejudicial to administration of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other conduct reflecting on practitioner's fitness — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must avoid other conduct that adversely reflects on fitness to practice before the USPTO; OED alleges that the acts and omissions described (to the extent not covered by specific provisions) violate 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residual catch-all for conduct not fitting a specific rule but that nonetheless reflects poorly on a practitioner's fitness to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for reinstatement — presumptions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that, if and when she applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume that (a) the allegations are true, and (b) she could not have successfully defended herself against the alleged violations (listed §§ 11.101, 11.103, 11.503(a)/(b), 11.804(c)/(d)/(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit of Resignation conditions the reinstatement process by creating statutory presumptions disadvantaging the respondent upon any future petition to reinstate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with suspension/exclusion notice rules — 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (rules concerning suspension or disbarment), including specific notice and other obligations described in the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order spells out how respondent may satisfy notice obligations for foreign-domiciled clients (emailing translated Final Order to client email addresses or via referring entity with specified reasonable measures) and requires details be set forth in the respondent's affidavit under § 11.58(d) and any reinstatement petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to foreign-domiciled clients: translation and email requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may satisfy obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c)(3)(i) for foreign-domiciled clients by emailing a copy of the Final Order correctly translated into the client's native language to: (1) the email in the 'Applicant's Information' if it belongs to the client and is reasonably believed to be directly accessible by the client; (2) an email belonging to the client that respondent reasonably believes the client directly accesses; or (3) to the foreign referring entity only if respondent takes reasonable measures to ensure the entity promptly forwards the email to the client, respondent is copied, respondent learns that the client actually received it, and the respondent's affidavit/petition details those measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order prescribes detailed steps and evidentiary requirements to satisfy notice obligations for foreign clients; forwarding via referring entity is allowed only with specified safeguards and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for 30 days to conclude pending matters — 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be granted limited recognition pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f) for thirty (30) days starting on the date of the Final Order so respondent may endeavor to conclude work on behalf of clients on matters pending before the Office; if work cannot be concluded within 30 days, respondent shall so advise each client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is time-limited and intended solely to allow winding down of active matters; respondent must notify clients if additional time/arrangements are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO.gov account disabling/suspension after limited recognition expires
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective the expiration of the 30-day limited recognition, USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to respondent; respondent shall not apply for, obtain, verify, sponsor, or have her name added to any USPTO.gov account for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order authorizes disabling accounts and places express prohibitions on account creation/verification/sponsorship by the respondent until reinstatement; re-enabling suspended accounts is not automatic upon reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using or assisting others to use USPTO filing systems after limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately upon expiration of the 30-day period of limited recognition, respondent is prohibited from using, accessing, or assisting others in using any USPTO.gov account(s) or other USPTO filing systems for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad prohibition to prevent continued practice through accounts or proxies once limited recognition period ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for re-enabling or creating USPTO.gov accounts post-reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if reinstated, nothing requires USPTO to re-enable or unsuspend any USPTO.gov account disabled under the Final Order; respondent is responsible for contacting the appropriate USPTO business unit to re-enable or for acquiring/creating a new account in accordance with USPTO policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement does not guarantee restoration of electronic access; respondent must undertake separate steps to regain account access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice of exclusion on consent text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is mandatory and intended to give public notice of the exclusion and its terms; the Official Gazette notice text is specified to be materially consistent with the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any reinstatement request
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reinstatement petition must satisfy the procedural and substantive requirements of § 11.60; the Final Order imposes this as an ongoing condition.
